note: Seed options for the Card Steering Board (https://claude.ai/artifact/XuXp2GMawpsNjLJV3wNp37). Written to the board's 'options' collection by Claude. Evidence notes point to research-notes.md.

items.title: Slow push-in portrait loop
items.detail: A 5-second camera push-in on Phill's real portrait, looping silently at the top of the card. Made with Higgsfield's image-to-video camera presets, then saved to our own hosting.
items.evidence: Higgsfield DoP makes 3 or 5 s clips from one photo with camera presets [VERIFIED]. Cost per take is an estimate [INFERENCE].

items.title: Greeting in Phill's real voice
items.detail: Phill records one welcome line himself. Higgsfield lip-syncs his real recording to his portrait. No voice cloning, so nothing of his voice is handed over for training.
items.evidence: Lipsync Studio animates a photo from supplied audio; keep under 30 s [VERIFIED].

items.title: Talking greeting in a cloned voice
items.detail: Clone Phill's voice once, then make new greetings from typed scripts (one per event or business). Faster to update, but Higgsfield may use uploads for training unless deleted, and lip detail can blur.
items.evidence: Voice clone costs 40 credits (US$2) [VERIFIED]. Training-use clause ToS §4.4 [VERIFIED by research agent].

items.needs: Real job photos you may share
items.title: Before-and-after job reel
items.detail: A 15-second reel of real Disaster Recovery jobs: the damage, the work, the result. Proof beats claims, and it fits the 'show proof of your work' advice on the card.
items.evidence: The card proposal's Discover example is showing proof of a real job [VERIFIED: PDF p.4].

items.needs: Photos of a physical card or logo
items.title: Spinning 3D card
items.detail: A 3D model of the physical card or the logo that people can spin with a finger. Higgsfield has image-to-3D jobs. Better for an object than for Phill's face.
items.evidence: image_to_3d and multi_image_to_3d job types in Higgsfield's CLI [VERIFIED]; cost and output format [UNCONFIRMED].

items.title: A consistent 'Phill' character for future clips
items.detail: Train Higgsfield's Soul ID on Phill's real photos so every future clip shows the same face. Powerful for marketing at scale, but it creates a reusable likeness: decide later.
items.evidence: Soul ID keeps a consistent face across clips [VERIFIED: Higgsfield help centre].

items.title: Trade-show mode
items.detail: On show days the card leads with the event: your stand, your talk time, the rabbit hunt. After the show it switches back on its own.
items.evidence: Phill's Brisbane and Melbourne shows [VERIFIED: his email 19/10].

items.title: Discover: one practical idea
items.detail: Four needs, each with one thing to do this week. In the prototype as drafts awaiting Phill's approval.
items.evidence: From the proposal's Discover door [VERIFIED: PDF p.4].

items.title: Spin, tap, review in their own words
items.detail: A fun spin opens the experience and reveals a tip or a thank-you, never a prize for reviewing. The customer taps three or four neutral answers about their real job. If they want, AI words a draft from their own answers, keeping any criticism. They edit it, pick their own stars, and one tap opens Google's own review page where they post it from their own account.
items.evidence: Google allows asking 'without offering incentives ... or attempting to influence the rating or the contents' [VERIFIED: support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114].

items.title: The right business, every time
items.detail: The card knows which business did the job (Disaster Recovery, CARSI, RestoreAssist) and opens that business's Google review form.
items.evidence: Google's own write-review link format [see research-notes.md].

items.title: Ask everyone, and offer a private line too
items.detail: Every customer gets the same invitation. Anyone can also send private feedback to the owner, always alongside the public review option, never instead of it.
items.evidence: Review gating (asking only happy customers) breaks Google's rules [see research-notes.md].

items.title: Pre-written five-star review, prize spin, posted for them
items.detail: As first described: we write the perfect review, a prize spin rewards it, and it posts through the customer's Gmail. Not being built: incentives, ghost-written reviews and posting for someone break Google's and the ACCC's rules and can get a Business Profile restricted.
items.evidence: See research-notes.md for the exact policy lines.

items.title: Same review engine for every card buyer
items.detail: Each buyer's card gets the rule-safe review flow pointed at their own business. A headline selling point for the AUD $249 tier.
items.evidence: Product sketch tier 3 [VERIFIED: product-sketch.md].
